author: opus-5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Review findings on 0aa2d025 fixed in f14eddf6: held rows are looked up at the thread's turn, not copied at enqueue; they count only against an exact count of at most 50, matched exactly, with the newest held reply no older than updated_at; a longer thread is read. Also: allowlist checked at the turn and before filing; at most 64 pending per channel (global cap 1,024); per-channel wake-up. Each counted in tests/thread_naming_reads.rs. Accepted and documented (module doc, README): an edit with nothing pushed inside read-ahead's 30 s still names a thread from the old text. Not done here: threads of more than 50 replies always cost a read even when the reader has their newest page open; the 10-min pause is triggered only by naming's own reads; batching a channel's due threads into one call is W14. Unverified: not measured against the live bridge.

author: opus-5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Re-review findings on 8475c79b fixed in 7788858e, with the per-channel queue cap pinned in 04bb66c1. A queued thread's naming is decided at its turn against the newest summary any page has carried of it (refreshed by every page), never the copy taken at enqueue: the root comes only from read-ahead, so a pushed edit or delete of it sends the thread to a read; the count is used only if read in the last 30 s, from a page without as_of, and no earlier than any reply held; a renamed thread rides deltas as the newest page showed it; a thread a delta removes is not carried and is named only from a read; a sentence is filed at the count of the messages it was written from. The re-review probes N1, N2, N2b, N3, N4, N5 are tests in tests/thread_naming_reads.rs, with five more; each new check removed alone fails a test. Accepted and documented (module doc, README): a change nobody pushed in the 30 s a row is held, edit or delete, can still reach a name (a deleted reply among the rows, or a deleted thread named). Costs reads: a Flat page read after the thread list, and a list carrying as_of, save none. Not done here: the 30 s age limit on the count is unit-tested only (read-ahead keeps the wall clock); a renamed thread whose root delete is pushed through ingest still rides deltas for up to 15 min, as before this branch; threads of more than 50 replies always cost a read; the 10-min pause is triggered only by naming's own reads; batching is W14. Unverified: not measured against the live bridge.
